quote: You have a right to action, but never to its fruits.
My followers shall never eat meat or drink intoxicants, even in the gravest calamity.
Keep the company of true sadhus; their association destroys sin and kindles bhakti.
The soul is never born, nor does it ever die.
They shall never steal, even a blade of grass that belongs to another.
Worship God with a sincere heart; He looks not at wealth, but at devotion.
Perform your duty established in yoga, abandoning attachment. Equanimity is yoga.
They shall never speak of the faults of others, nor listen to such talk.
One should never abandon dharma, even at the cost of one’s life.
Whenever dharma declines and adharma rises, I manifest Myself.
Ahinsa is the highest dharma.
Svadharma, atma-gnan, vairagya, and bhakti coupled with Bhagvan’s greatness.
They shall donate a tenth, or at least a twentieth, of their earnings in the service of God.
Serve cows, sadhus and the poor; such seva pleases God.
A person must elevate himself by his own mind, and not degrade himself.
They shall arise daily before sunrise, remember Shri Krishna, and then begin the day’s duties.
Nilkanth Varni walked the land in tapas so that dharma might live in every heart.
If one offers Me with love a leaf, a flower, a fruit, or water, I accept that offering.
They shall wear a kanthi of tulsi around the neck and apply a tilak of gopichandan.
Daily puja, darshan and the remembrance of God’s form keep the mind pure.
Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give, do it as an offering to Me.
They shall worship Shri Krishna with devotion, offering the sixteen upachars.
Wicked company darkens the heart; satsang makes it shine.
To those who are constantly devoted and who worship Me with love, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have.
Dharma, jnana, vairagya and bhakti — these four are the means to moksha.
Hold fast to the niyams given by Maharaj; they are the fence around bhakti.
I am the Self, seated in the hearts of all beings.
Bhakti of God should always be practised together with dharma.
Where the sadhu sits, there God is pleased to dwell.
Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, worship Me and bow to Me.
They shall never abandon the dharma of their own ashrama.
Speak the truth, keep the body in brahmacharya, and let the mind rest in God.
He who has no hatred for any being, who is friendly and compassionate, is dear to Me.
Understand Narayan and Shiva as one; do not see difference between them.
Compassion for every living being is the mark of a true satsangi.
Better one’s own dharma, though imperfect, than the dharma of another well performed.
They shall observe the Ekadashi fasts and the birth festivals of Shri Krishna.
Remember God’s murti at dawn and at dusk; the day then becomes seva.
The wise see the same in a learned brahmana, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and one who cooks dogs.
They shall never listen to scriptures or katha that oppose Vishnu.
Pride is the thief of bhakti; humility is its guardian.
From anger comes delusion; from delusion, loss of memory; from that, the ruin of understanding.
They shall never consume food that has not first been offered to God.
A house becomes a mandir when God’s name is spoken there each day.
For one who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, I am never lost, nor is he ever lost to Me.
My followers shall never kill any living being, not even the smallest insect.
The glory of satsang is this: a sinner becomes a sadhu, and a sadhu becomes still more luminous.
Abandon all other dharmas and surrender unto Me alone. I shall free you from all sins. Do not fear.
Those who observe these commands shall attain happiness here and the highest bliss hereafter.
Bhagvan Swaminarayan walked as Nilkanth so that every village might know dharma, bhakti and fearlessness.
There is nothing higher than Me, O Arjun. All this is strung on Me like pearls on a thread.
They shall never speak a lie, except to save a life or protect dharma in a moment of crisis.
Let the mouth sing kirtan, the hands do seva, and the mind rest at the lotus feet of Maharaj.
Work done as worship of the Lord from whom all beings come leads a person to perfection.
They shall have compassion for the poor, the afflicted and those in distress.
Do not delay dharma until tomorrow; the breath you hold now is the only wealth you truly own.
Always think of Me, be My devotee, worship Me and offer namaskar to Me. You will come to Me; I promise this.
None of my followers shall ever commit theft, adultery, or take what is not given.
Read the Shikshapatri, live the Vachnamrut, and walk as taught in the Satsangi Jeevan — that is satsang.
